entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation - Comprehensive Safety, Sustainability and Recycling Requirements
entries.summary: The EU Batteries Regulation covers sourcing, manufacturing, use, and recycling of batteries with comprehensive safety, sustainability, and recycling requirements. It includes 15 ambitious measures supporting the battery sector through significant capital and R&D funding through 2030.

entries.title: EU Minimum Recycled Content Rules and Battery Reusability Standards
entries.summary: New minimum recycled content requirements effective August 18, 2031: 16% cobalt, 85% lead, 6% lithium, and 6% nickel in batteries. Portable batteries must be sealed, weigh ≤5kg, and be easily removable with simple tools for recycling compliance.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation Implementation Phase - Phased Obligations 2025-2030s
entries.summary: As of 2026, the EU Battery Regulation is in full implementation phase with substantive obligations phased between 2025-2028. Requirements span carbon accounting, production obligations, material restrictions, and performance/durability standards for rechargeable industrial and EV batteries.

entries.title: E-Moped Battery Compliance - UNECE R136 and EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542
entries.summary: L-category vehicle batteries require UNECE R136 type approval and compliance with EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542 including labeling, durability classifications, and carbon-footprint disclosure. REESS safety tests cover short-circuit, overcharge, vibration, mechanical impact, and fire safety.

entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation Digital Battery Passport and Lifecycle Traceability
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation requires digital battery passport, traceability of raw materials, carbon footprint reporting, and lifecycle transparency spanning design, production, transport, use, and recycling. Focuses on safer batteries and responsible supply chains.

entries.title: Lithium Battery Transport Compliance - UN 38.3 Testing and SDS Requirements
entries.summary: Lithium batteries require valid UN 38.3 test reports from accredited labs (ISO/IEC 17025) and compliant Safety Data Sheets citing UN 3480, Class 9. Documentation must be current and match exact battery models for EU customs compliance.

entries.title: Joint Industry Guidance on Battery Manufacturer Definition
entries.summary: EUROBAT, EPBA, and Recharge released joint guidance clarifying manufacturer definition under EU Batteries Regulation with legal interpretation, key duties, and compliance examples supporting consistent application across the battery value chain.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Due Diligence Obligations - Enforcement Postponed to August 2027
entries.summary: EU has postponed enforcement of battery due diligence obligations from August 2025 to August 2027. Large companies placing batteries on the EU market must implement due diligence policies, digital traceability systems, supplier risk assessments, grievance mechanisms, and public reporting. Supply chain mapping remains the biggest challenge as most companies lack visibility beyond tier two suppliers.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation Chapter VII - Supply Chain Due Diligence Requirements
entries.summary: Chapter VII of the EU Battery Regulation applies from August 18, 2027, imposing due diligence obligations on economic operators placing batteries on the market. Companies must establish risk-based environmental and human rights due diligence policies for cobalt, natural graphite, lithium, and nickel sourcing for batteries above 2 kWh capacity, and establish UNGP-based grievance mechanisms.

entries.title: EU Battery Passport and Digital Traceability Requirements - February 2027
entries.summary: Starting February 2027, batteries must have a Battery Passport containing lifecycle information including manufacturing data, carbon footprint data, and recycled material content. Supply chain due diligence requirements take effect August 2027, requiring companies to implement systems for responsible sourcing and supply chain transparency.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 - Lifecycle Regulation and Market Access Requirements
entries.summary: EU Battery Regulation governs batteries across their entire lifecycle from raw material sourcing through manufacturing, market implementation, use-phase performance, to repurposing and recycling. It integrates sustainability metrics, carbon accounting, supply chain due diligence, and digital traceability as direct market access requirements, aligning with Circular Economy Action Plan and climate neutrality objectives.

entries.title: EU Battery Passport Documentation Requirements - Supply Chain Due Diligence Reports
entries.summary: Companies must document supply chain due-diligence reports describing due-diligence policies, risk-management processes, verification activities, and third-party supply chain assurances. EU Taxonomy disclosure statements and sustainability report availability must be provided as part of battery passport requirements.

entries.title: RoHS 2026 Exemption Structure Transformation - Pack 22 Updates
entries.summary: The EU RoHS landscape is undergoing significant structural transformation in 2026, phasing out broad exemptions in favor of narrower, application-specific sub-entries. The European Commission has finalized a strategy to phase out general lead exemptions through granular Pack 22 updates, requiring compliance professionals to manage a rapidly fragmenting list of technical exemptions.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Removability and Replaceability Requirements
entries.summary: Article 11 requirements of the EU Battery Regulation enter into force on February 18, 2027, stipulating that portable batteries in appliances must be readily removable and replaceable by end users or independent professionals. The regulation also maintains and updates restrictions on hazardous substances including mercury, cadmium, and lead with new exemptions and review clauses.

entries.title: ECHA February 2026 REACH SVHC Candidate List Update
entries.summary: The European Chemicals Agency published an update to the REACH Candidate List of Substances of Very High Concern (SVHC) on February 4, 2026, adding two new substances for a total of 253 entries. Suppliers must inform downstream users and consumers if an SVHC is present in articles above 0.1% weight by weight and have notification duties to ECHA.

entries.title: RoHS Exemptions - Nine Key Changes and Stricter Limits
entries.summary: Proposed changes affecting nine critical RoHS exemptions include stricter limits on lead in electronic solders, cadmium in batteries, and hexavalent chromium in surface coatings, with shorter duration of exemptions. These changes require manufacturers to prepare for more restrictive material usage and compliance timelines.

entries.title: EU WEEE Directive Review - Circular Economy Act
entries.summary: The European Commission is expected to review the WEEE framework in 2026 as part of the upcoming Circular Economy Act. The WEEE Directive was originally adopted in 2002 and last updated in 2012.

entries.title: WEEE Regulations Amendment 2025 - Online Marketplace Operators
entries.summary: The 2025 WEEE Amendments establish online marketplace operators as producers for EEE supplied by non-UK sellers via their platforms, making marketplaces responsible for WEEE registration and financing. A new vapes category (7.1) has been added to the WEEE classification.

entries.title: 2026 WEEE Overhaul - Extended Producer Responsibility Update
entries.summary: Europe's 2026 WEEE revision represents a complete accountability overhaul for the electronics industry, addressing the 25-point gap between current 40% recovery rates and the 65% target. Cross-border online sales compliance gaps are being addressed through updated frameworks.

entries.title: Swedish WEEE Regulation Implementation
entries.summary: New Swedish WEEE regulations come into force on 12 August 2026, replacing current Swedish regulations. Some provisions will apply at later dates.

entries.title: EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) - Articles 3.3(d), (e), (f) Cybersecurity Requirements
entries.summary: As of August 1, 2025, Articles 3.3(d), (e), and (f) of the Radio Equipment Directive (RED) are mandatory for wireless-connected devices sold in the EU. These essential cybersecurity requirements apply to all wireless devices from smartphones to IoT equipment requiring CE marking compliance.

entries.summary: EN 18031 series compliance is mandatory for all internet-connected radio equipment placed on EU market since August 1, 2025. The three-part standard covers network protection (EN 18031-1), personal data protection (EN 18031-2), and financial transaction security (EN 18031-3).

entries.title: Europe's WEEE Revision: 2026 Overhaul
entries.summary: Major WEEE directive revision planned for 2026 addressing accountability gaps in electronics industry. Current EU recovery rate is only 40% against a 65% target, with cross-border online sales creating significant compliance gaps. entries.title: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Directive (WEEE) - 2012/19/EU
entries.summary: Revised WEEE Directive (2012/19/EU) enhances collection and recycling rates for electronic waste with broadened scope and updated definitions. Directive reflects EU's emphasis on sustainability and circular economy principles with improved treatment requirements.

entries.title: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (Amendment, etc.) Regulations 2025 - UK
entries.summary: UK WEEE Regulations amended in 2025 introducing new obligations for online marketplace operators, creating new product category for vapes, and updating import/export classification requirements. Enforcement by Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS).

new_entries.title: RoHS 3 - Extended Substance Restrictions Including Phthalates
new_entries.summary: RoHS 3 amendment expands restricted substances to include four phthalates (DEHP, BBP, DBP, DIBP) with maximum concentration limits of 0.1% by weight per homogeneous material, except cadmium at 0.01%.

entries.title: USB-C Common Charging Standard for Laptops - Implementation Deadline
entries.summary: EU requirement mandating USB-C as the common charging standard for laptops effective April 28, 2026. This extends the USB-C standardization already applied to other consumer devices across the EU market.

entries.title: EU Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) - Digital Product Passport
entries.summary: EU regulation effective January 2026 mandating all accessories sold in the European Economic Area publish a Digital Product Passport (DPP). Regulation requires documentation of service life, repairability, and material traceability for compliance.

entries.title: Battery Replaceability Requirements - Electronic Devices
entries.summary: EU requirement effective February 18, 2027 mandating that electronic devices sold in the EU must have easily replaceable batteries. Aims to extend device lifecycle and reduce electronic waste.

entries.title: Council of the European Union eases rules on replacing damaged charging cables
entries.summary: The new measuring instruments directive sets common standards for electric chargers and gas dispensers, clearing the path for widespread deployment of charging infrastructure in Europe. This directive is part of Europe's transition to a greener and more energy-efficient mobility system.

entries.title: EU Tightens Rules on Reusing and Recycling Materials - EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542
entries.summary: In 2026, new provisions of EU Regulation 2023/1542 come into force imposing stricter labelling requirements including 'non-rechargeable' marking and duration of use. Higher collection targets (73% for portable batteries by 2030) and recycling efficiency targets (90% for key metals, 50% for lithium by 31.12.2027) are mandated to promote circular economy.

entries.title: The European Battery Regulation and Digital Framework - EU 2023/1542
entries.summary: Regulation EU 2023/1542 replaces Directive 2006/66/EC and establishes new sustainability and recycling requirements. entries.title: EU Battery Regulations: Sustainability Goals, Stricter Safety Standards, and Reporting Obligations
entries.summary: Recent EU battery regulations raise recycling rates and demand minimum recycled content of new batteries. entries.title: EU RED & EN 18031 Compliance Guide: IoT Cybersecurity 2025
entries.summary: Comprehensive guide covering new EU Radio Equipment Directive cybersecurity requirements effective from 2025. entries.title: EN 18031 Compliance: 2026 Guide for Connected Products
entries.summary: Details EN 18031 series consisting of three standards covering network protection (EN 18031-1), personal data protection (EN 18031-2), and financial transaction security (EN 18031-3). entries.title: EU Harmonizes Cybersecurity Standards for Radio Equipment Under EN 18031 Series
entries.summary: Outlines three EN 18031:2024 standards with implementation implications for manufacturers. Key compliance date of August 1, 2025 for all radio equipment to meet new cybersecurity requirements under the Radio Equipment Directive.

entries.title: EN 18031 | Cybersecurity Standard for Radio Equipment
entries.summary: Explains EN 18031-1 general cybersecurity requirements for all internet-connected radio equipment, ensuring network protections against unauthorized access and malicious interference. Applicable across all industries using wireless or connected devices.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive Cybersecurity Testing – EN 18031
entries.summary: BSI guidance on EN 18031 cybersecurity testing requirements for radio equipment including Wi-Fi routers, Bluetooth devices, and automotive components. Identifies exempt non-connected radio equipment and testing scope.

entries.title: EN 18031 Cybersecurity Testing for the Radio Equipment Directive (RED)
entries.summary: Details Delegated Regulation 2022/30/EU cybersecurity requirements under the Radio Equipment Directive, effective August 1, 2025. Addresses cyber threats and mandatory compliance for all radio-enabled equipment sold in the EU.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive
entries.summary: Overview of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 active since August 1, 2025, requiring all radio equipment to comply with binding cybersecurity requirements. Highlights application of harmonized standards EN 18031-1/2/3 and risks of non-compliance.

entries.title: EN 18031 Cybersecurity Testing for CE Radio Equipment under RED
entries.summary: Explains Radio Equipment Directive requirements and mandatory cybersecurity for CE marking since August 2025. Covers essential requirements for Articles 3(3)(d), 3(3)(e), and 3(3)(f) addressing network protection, privacy, and fraud prevention.

entries.title: EN 18031 – Cybersecurity testing of radio equipment
entries.summary: Confirms mandatory compliance with EN 18031-x requirements for all affected devices from August 1, 2025 to continue sales on European market. Emphasizes timely implementation of new safety standards.

entries.title: RED 3.3: Cybersecurity Update to EU Radio Equipment Directive
entries.summary: The Radio Equipment Directive was updated to include cybersecurity requirements under Article 3.3. This major update marks a significant step in the EU's digital product regulation, affecting almost every connected product on the market alongside the Cyber Resilience Act and Digital Product Passport.

entries.title: RED Directive: Cybersecurity Requirements for 4G/5G Repeaters
entries.summary: The RED Directive now requires 4G/5G repeaters to implement security-by-design measures, secure data protection with encrypted communications, and secure access management. These cybersecurity requirements directly apply to repeaters deployed in professional and industrial environments where data confidentiality is critical.

entries.title: EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2025 - RedCap Certification Paths
entries.summary: The revised Radio Equipment Directive 2025 includes specific certification paths for RedCap device interoperability and security. The directive works in conjunction with the EU Cyber Resilience Act to create mandatory security requirements for connected 5G devices.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive (RED) - Compliance Requirements for GSM/4G/5G Devices
entries.summary: Cellular and mobile devices with 4G/LTE/5G must comply with EN 301 EMC standards and other harmonized standards. Products including smartphones, tablets, and 4G/5G mobile routers require RED lab testing to verify compliance before entering the EU market.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive (RED) - Mandatory Compliance for EU Market
entries.summary: The Radio Equipment Directive is one of the most critical regulatory instruments for placing electronic products on the market. Confirmation of conformity is mandatory for manufacturers or authorized representatives to import products into the EU and legally distribute them.

entries.title: Implementation Decision (EU) 2025/2499 - RED Harmonized Standards Update
entries.summary: The European Commission published Implementation Decision (EU) 2025/2499 revising RED harmonized standards for short-range devices and airborne mobile communication systems. This update reflects evolving technical requirements for radio equipment compliance.

entries.title: RED Cybersecurity Compliance: EN 18031 Evaluation Services
entries.summary: TÜV SÜD announces mandatory RED cybersecurity compliance requirements (Article 3.3 d, e, f) now in force for wireless and connected devices entering the EU market. The organization provides EN 18031 evaluation, RED assessment, and notified body services for CE marking and EU market access.

entries.title: Security Features on CC2674 / CC13x4 Devices - EN 18031 Compliance
entries.summary: Texas Instruments documents security features for Bluetooth LE devices targeting EN 18031 compliance (effective August 1, 2025) and upcoming Cyber Resilience Act requirements. CC27xx family devices recommended for BLE applications requiring secure key storage and hardware-based security isolation.

entries.title: BLE PAwR ESL: Complete Guide to Developing Electronic Shelf Labels
entries.summary: Guidance on EN 18031 series harmonization for BLE-based electronic shelf label systems, noting that while individual ESL tags may not be internet-connected, complete systems with access points and backends may fall under cybersecurity obligations for personal data and remote access functionality.

entries.title: EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) - New Cybersecurity Requirements under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30
entries.summary: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 activates essential cybersecurity requirements under RED Articles 3.3(d), (e), and (f) for internet-connectable devices, devices processing personal data, or facilitating value transfers. Requirements include preventing network harm, protecting personal data and privacy, and protecting against fraud. Applicable harmonized standard is EN 18031 series.

entries.title: EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) - Cybersecurity Requirements for IP Audio and Networked Systems
entries.summary: Effective August 1, 2025, RED Articles 3.3(d), (e), and (f) enforce cybersecurity requirements via Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30. Products must not harm networks, must incorporate safeguards for personal data protection, and must protect against fraud. Applies to IP audio amplifiers, network audio endpoints, SIP intercoms, and IP PA controllers using harmonized standard EN 18031 series.

entries.title: ETSI EN 300 328 and EN 301 489 - 2.4 GHz Radio Equipment Compliance Standards
entries.summary: ETSI EN 300 328 governs spectrum usage in the 2.4 GHz ISM band under RED Article 3.2, while ETSI EN 301 489-1 and EN 301 489-17 specify EMC requirements for wideband equipment including Wi-Fi and Bluetooth under RED Article 3.1(b). EN 62368-1 covers safety requirements for audio, video, IT, and communication equipment under RED Article 3.1(a).

entries.title: ETSI EN 301 489 Testing and Accreditation for Radio Equipment Directive Compliance
entries.summary: Accredited EMC testing for radio equipment under RED Article 3.1(b) covering ETSI EN 301 489-1, EN 301 489-3, and EN 301 489-17 for short range devices, broadband data (WiFi/Bluetooth), and wireless audio. Testing combines emissions and immunity with EN 300 series radio performance requirements.

entries.title: EU Tightens Rules on Reusing and Recycling Materials - Batteries Regulation
entries.summary: EU Batteries Regulation establishes minimum recycled content requirements starting August 18, 2031 (16% cobalt, 85% lead, 6% lithium, 6% nickel). Batteries must be easily removable and recyclable, with portable batteries requiring sealing and simple tool removal. The Commission will review recycling targets every five years beginning in 2026.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Digital Battery Passport and Lifecycle Requirements
entries.summary: EU Battery Regulation mandates traceability of raw materials, carbon footprint reporting, and digital battery passport implementation to track key battery information across entire lifecycle. Requirements cover battery design, production, transportation, use, and recycling with enhanced transparency standards.

entries.title: EU Customs Compliance for Lithium Batteries - UN 3480/3481 Classification and Documentation
entries.summary: Lithium batteries require proper UN 3480 (lithium-ion) or UN 3481 (lithium-metal) classification based on watt-hour ratings, not mAh. Documentation must include UN 38.3 test reports from accredited labs, battery safety data sheets with Section 14 transport information, and proper hazard classification (Class 9, PG II for power banks >100Wh).

entries.title: HS Code Classification for EV Batteries - EU TARIC Database Requirements
entries.summary: Lithium-ion EV batteries fall under HS code 8507.60. Importers must use exact codes from EU TARIC database rather than supplier codes to avoid incorrect duty rates and fines. Standard EU import taxes range from 1.9-3.7%, with additional 19% VAT in Germany.

entries.title: EUROBAT Manufacturer Definition Guidance - EU Batteries Regulation Compliance
entries.summary: EUROBAT, EPBA, and Recharge released joint industry guidance clarifying manufacturer definition under EU Batteries Regulation, covering legal interpretation, key duties, and compliance examples to support consistent application across battery value chain.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542: Lifecycle Emissions & Supply Chain Due Diligence
entries.summary: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 integrates lifecycle emissions, recycled material content, supply chain due diligence and end-of-life recovery. From 2027, batteries on the EU market must carry a QR code connected to a Digital Battery Passport with structured technical and sustainability data, requiring verifiable sources for all figures.

entries.title: ESG Quick Guide: EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation - Due Diligence Requirements
entries.summary: Comprehensive guide on Chapter VII due diligence elements of EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation 2023/1542 (as amended by Omnibus IV). Covers requirements on economic operators placing batteries on the EU market regarding sustainability, safety, labelling, and supply chain due diligence.

entries.title: The Real Stakes for Compliance Professionals With the EU Battery Regulation
entries.summary: Lifecycle regulation governs batteries from raw material sourcing through recycling. Battery regulation now integrates sustainability metrics, carbon accounting, supply chain due diligence, and digital traceability into market access requirements, aligning with Circular Economy Action Plan and climate neutrality objectives.

entries.title: Supply Chain Due Diligence for Batteries: 2025 Market Analysis
entries.summary: EU Battery Regulation continues shaping corporate priorities despite two-year postponement of due diligence obligations. Economic operators face pressure to prepare for mandatory supply chain due diligence in challenging market environment with budget constraints.

entries.title: The European Battery Regulation and Digital Battery Passport: Lifecycle Governance
entries.summary: Addresses lifecycle governance including battery reuse, repurposing, traceability, and producer responsibility. Discusses regulatory requirements for Battery Passports, sustainability due diligence obligations, and extended producer responsibility with extraterritorial effects on global battery value chains.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation Timeline: 2025-2028 Compliance Milestones
entries.summary: Regulatory timeline for EU battery compliance: 2025 supply-chain due diligence begins; 2026 carbon footprint reporting starts; 2027 (February 18) Battery Passport mandatory; 2028 lifecycle impact assessments required. Critical deadlines for manufacturers and economic operators.

entries.title: Digital Battery Passport: February 2027 Mandatory Implementation
entries.summary: From February 2027, all batteries placed on EU market must carry digital passport with verified sustainability and supply-chain information. Concept will expand to other product categories under upcoming Circular Economy Act and EU Product Act.

entries.title: Exporting Batteries to EU: 2026 Documentation & Labeling Guide
entries.summary: Mandatory 2026 rules for non-EU exporters exporting batteries to EU market under Regulation 2023/1542. Covers carbon footprint documentation, labeling shifts, and BMS data access requirements for compliance.

entries.summary: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 treats batteries as general products requiring detailed, verified information throughout lifecycle. entries.summary: Industry summit addressing convergence of chemicals policy, product compliance, and circularity requirements. new_entries.title: WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU - Open Scope Implementation
new_entries.summary: The WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU entered open scope on 15 August 2018, making all electrical and electronic equipment subject to compulsory registration. This represents a fundamental shift in the scope of WEEE compliance across EU member states.

new_entries.title: EU WEEE Directive - PV Module Recycling and EPR Framework Reform
new_entries.summary: Recent analysis calls for urgent reform of EU WEEE Directive to address PV module recycling gaps, including strengthened EPR frameworks, harmonized fee structures, and mandatory reporting procedures. Implementation remains fragmented across member states despite PV inclusion since 2012.

new_entries.title: WEEE Evidence and National Protocols Guidance - UK
new_entries.summary: Updated UK guidance on WEEE evidence requirements for proof of reuse or treatment by approved facilities and exports. Provides national protocols for compliance with WEEE regulations.

new_entries.title: Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) - WEEE Directive Alignment
new_entries.summary: DIGITALEUROPE position on amending CRMA to address regulatory overlaps with WEEE Directive, particularly regarding exemptions for medical devices that cannot be safely dismantled. Recommends harmonizing exemptions between CRMA and WEEE Directive Article 2.

entries.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 — New Ecodesign Rules for Chargers, Cables & Power Supplies
entries.summary: The European Commission adopted Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 on October 13, 2025, introducing significantly stricter ecodesign requirements for external power supplies, wireless chargers, battery chargers, and USB-C cables. The regulation mandates higher energy efficiency standards, detachable cables, USB Type-C ports on chargers, and introduces a mandatory 'Common Charger' logo, with manufacturers having 3 years to comply.

entries.title: EU Rolls Out Updated Ecodesign Rules for USB-C and Wireless Chargers by 2028
entries.summary: The European Commission introduced updated ecodesign rules for external power supplies and chargers, expanding requirements to wireless and USB-C types with stricter efficiency standards and mandatory detachable cables by 2028. The regulation targets approximately 400 million external power supplies sold annually in the EU.

entries.title: Single Charger in the EU: New Regulation on USB-C Mandatory on Charger Side
entries.summary: The new 2025 ecodesign regulation for external power supplies mandates USB-C ports on both the charging device and charger body, completing the common charger initiative started with the 2022 directive. The regulation also covers wireless chargers and cables, introducing a 'Common Charger' logo for consumer transparency.

entries.title: EU Issues New Ecodesign Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 for External Power Supplies
entries.summary: EU Regulation 2025/2052 establishes new minimum energy efficiency and maximum no-load power consumption requirements, standby power limits for wireless chargers, mandatory USB-C ports with detachable cables, and a 'Common Charger' logo. Additional requirements include surge-resistibility testing and labeling updates on packaging and nameplates.

entries.title: Updated Draft of Ecodesign Requirements for External Power Supplies
entries.summary: On March 2, 2025, the European Commission published a revised draft regulation on ecodesign requirements for external power supplies, extending scope to USB Type-C cables with energy loss limits and connector labeling. The regulation introduces a 'Common Charger' logo to inform consumers of interoperability across different devices.

entries.title: EU Regulation 2025/2052 Ecodesign - Key Requirements
entries.summary: EU Regulation 2025/2052 mandates mandatory USB Type-C sockets on external power supplies, bans fixed 'captive cables' in favor of detachable cables, and requires USB-PD protocol compliance. A specific 'Common Charger' EU logo must be affixed to power supply labels and product packaging to inform consumers of compatibility.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 - Full Implementation and Compliance Obligations
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 replaces Directive 2006/66/EC and introduces stricter requirements for battery safety, sustainability, transparency, and lifecycle management. Key compliance deadlines include digital battery passport implementation by February 2027 and recycled content declaration requirements from 2028, with mandatory minimums from 2030.

entries.title: Digital Battery Passport Implementation - February 2027 Deadline
entries.summary: Companies must make comprehensive information about batteries available digitally throughout their entire lifecycle starting February 2027 under EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. This applies to electric vehicle batteries, light means of transport batteries, and industrial batteries across all EU markets.

entries.title: Lithium Material Recovery Targets - 2027 and 2031 Deadlines
entries.summary: EU Battery Regulation Article 71(3)(e) establishes lithium material recovery requirements of 50% by 2027 and 80% by 2031. Recycled content declaration becomes mandatory from 2028 with minimum thresholds enforced from 2030 across all battery chemistries.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation Recycling Efficiency and Material Recovery Rates Methodology
entries.summary: EUROBAT position paper proposes improvements to the draft delegated act regarding methodology for calculating recycling efficiencies and material recovery rates under the EU Battery Regulation. This guidance supports compliance with recycling and sustainability targets.

entries.title: Battery Directive Repeal and Transition to EU Battery Regulation
entries.summary: Directive 2006/66/EC will be fully repealed in 2027, with 2026 marking intensified EU rules requiring batteries to be more durable, safer, and easier to recycle. The transition supports circular economy objectives and aligns with projected tenfold battery demand increase by 2030.

entries.title: UNECE R136 and EU Batteries Regulation for E-Mobility Compliance
entries.summary: L-category vehicles require UNECE R136 type approval for electric powertrains and REESS (Rechargeable Energy Storage System) testing, combined with EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542 lifecycle obligations including labeling, durability classifications, and carbon-footprint disclosure.

entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation - Minimum Recycled Content Requirements
entries.summary: EU Batteries Regulation establishes minimum recycled content requirements effective August 18, 2031, including 16% cobalt, 85% lead, 6% lithium, and 6% nickel for industrial, SLI, and EV batteries. Portable batteries must be sealed, weigh maximum 5kg, and be easily removable with simple tools. European Commission will review recycling targets every five years starting in 2026.

entries.title: Joint Industry Guidance on Battery Manufacturer Definition under EU Batteries Regulation
entries.summary: EUROBAT, EPBA, and Recharge released joint guidance clarifying the manufacturer definition under EU Batteries Regulation, covering legal interpretation, key duties, and compliance examples. This guidance supports consistent compliance across the battery value chain.

entries.title: Lithium Battery Classification and UN Handling Requirements for EU Customs
entries.summary: Portable chargers and lithium-ion batteries must be classified under UN 3480 (lithium-ion) and UN 3481 (lithium-metal) by watt-hour (Wh) rating. Devices exceeding 100Wh require special handling. Many shipments are flagged at EU borders due to incorrect mAh-only labeling without Wh conversion.

entries.title: EU End-of-Life Vehicle (ELV) Directive - Expanded Scope for Lithium-Ion Batteries
entries.summary: Draft ELV Directive significantly expands scope to include heavy-duty vehicles, electric and hybrid vehicles, with explicit emphasis on lithium-ion batteries and electronic components. New directive incorporates circular economy approaches including reuse, refurbishment, repair, and redistribution.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Due Diligence Obligations - Postponement to August 2027
entries.summary: The EU has postponed enforcement of battery due diligence obligations from August 2025 to August 2027. Once in force, large companies placing batteries on the EU market must implement due diligence policies, digital traceability systems, supplier risk assessments, grievance mechanisms, and public reporting. Supply chain mapping remains the biggest challenge as most companies lack visibility beyond tier two suppliers.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Due Diligence Requires Traceability for Critical Materials
entries.summary: Meeting EU Battery Regulation due diligence obligations requires implementation of traceability systems for cobalt, natural graphite, lithium, and nickel supply chains by August 2025. Economic operators must implement systems to prove the provenance and material chain of custody for compliance verification.

entries.title: ESG Quick Guide: EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation - Due Diligence Requirements
entries.summary: Comprehensive guide on due diligence elements (Chapter VII) of the EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation 2023 as amended by Omnibus IV. The regulation imposes obligations on sustainability, safety, labelling, marking, information provision, and extended producer responsibility with top-level management oversight required for policy implementation.

entries.title: The Real Stakes for Compliance Professionals With the EU Battery Regulation
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation features lifecycle regulation governing batteries from raw material sourcing to recycling. It integrates sustainability metrics, carbon accounting, supply chain due diligence, and digital traceability as market access requirements, expanding scope beyond traditional waste and collection obligations.

entries.title: Supply Chain Due Diligence for Batteries - 2025 Market Analysis
entries.summary: Despite the two-year postponement of EU Battery Regulation due diligence obligations, economic operators face continued pressure to prepare for mandatory supply chain due diligence in a challenging market environment with budget constraints. entries.summary: Significant changes recommended for nine critical RoHS exemptions. Manufacturers need to review and update compliance strategies for affected product categories and exemption statuses.

entries.title: WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU - Open Scope Implementation
entries.summary: The WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU introduced open scope on 15 August 2018, making all electrical and electronic equipment subject to compulsory registration. This expanded the scope to include devices such as furniture and clothing with electrical functions, significantly increasing the number of regulated products compared to the previous 2002/96/EC directive.

entries.title: UK WEEE Regulations 2025 Amendment - Online Marketplace Operators
entries.summary: The Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (Amendment, etc.) Regulations 2025 introduced significant changes including the designation of online marketplace operators as producers. Additionally, from 1 January 2024, all vape retailers must accept used vapes from customers free of charge.

entries.title: EU Waste Shipment Rules - New Annex VII Digital Requirements
entries.summary: New EU waste shipment rules requiring digital submission of Annex VII forms come into force on 21 May 2026. The new format is designed for digital purposes and creates compliance challenges for smaller operators and those across multiple jurisdictions.

entries.title: UK Government WEEE Evidence and National Protocols Guidance Update
entries.summary: The UK Environment Agency updated guidance on waste electrical and electronic equipment, including recovery and recycling targets by category (e.g., 85% recovery, 80% recycling for large household appliances). entries.title: EU WEEE Directive Revision - Enhanced EPR Frameworks for PV Recycling
entries.summary: Reform of the EU WEEE Directive is needed to strengthen Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks with clearer PV-specific waste obligations, harmonised EPR fee structures, and mandatory reporting procedures. entries.title: EU Omnibus Directive - EPR Authorized Representatives Appointment Pause

entries.title: EU Common Charger Directive - USB-C Mandate for Electronic Devices
entries.summary: The Council and European Parliament reached a provisional political agreement on a directive introducing mandatory USB-C charging ports for a range of electronic devices. Implementation required 24 months after entry into force for most devices, with laptops compliant by April 28, 2026. The directive reduces e-waste by allowing consumers to purchase devices with or without chargers.

entries.title: EU Universal Charger Directive Implementation - April 28, 2026 Laptop Deadline
entries.summary: The European Union's Universal Charger Directive requires all portable electronic devices sold in the EU to use USB-C interfaces and be compatible with USB PD fast charging protocol. Laptops must complete compliance certification by April 28, 2026. The directive is now in implementation stage.

entries.title: EU Guidelines for the Interpretation of the Directive on Universal Chargers
entries.source: Official Journal of the European Union
entries.summary: EU Commission clarifies in C/2024/2997 that the RED (Radio Equipment Directive) requires USB-C ports only for cable-charged devices. Wireless charging and other methods remain permitted, with the Commission explicitly leaving room for monitoring technical developments and potential future regulatory action.

entries.title: External Power Supply Ecodesign Compliance - EU Regulations 2017
entries.summary: EU ecodesign regulations for external power supplies mandate compliance with energy efficiency requirements and proper WEEE waste disposal. Products must meet statutory instrument 2010 No. 2617 and EU ecodesign directives for energy-related products with CE/FCC/RoHS certifications.

entries.title: IEC 63652 Recognition of NFC Wireless Charging Standards
entries.summary: The IEC formally recognized NFC Wireless Charging under IEC 63652 as the international framework for sub-3W wireless power in small devices like smart glasses and wearables. The EU Common Charging Directive calls for harmonized wireless charging standards, positioning NFC as a foundation for future development.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 - Labelling and Collection Requirements
entries.summary: New provisions of EU Batteries Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 come into force in 2026, imposing stricter labelling requirements including 'non-rechargeable' marking and duration of use. Sets higher collection targets (73% for portable batteries by 2030) and recycling efficiency targets (90% for key metals, 50% for lithium by 31.12.2027).

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 - Digital Battery Passport Implementation
entries.summary: EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 comes into force from 18 February 2027 requiring mandatory unique Digital Battery Passport (DBP) for EV batteries and industrial batteries with capacity above 2kWh placed on EU market. Applies to all batteries and cells, replacing old Battery Directive with stricter requirements for safety, sustainability, and transparency.

entries.title: EU Measuring Instruments Directive - Harmonized Standards for Electric Chargers
entries.summary: Council of the European Union updates measuring instruments directive setting common standards for electric chargers and gas dispensers. Harmonized technical requirements support widespread deployment of charging infrastructure and Europe's transition to greener, energy-efficient mobility system.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Sustainability and Recycling Framework
entries.summary: Regulation EU 2023/1542 establishes transformative regulatory framework for batteries supporting sustainability, transparency, and circular economy. Replaces Directive 2006/66/EC with new sustainability and recycling requirements including carbon footprint evaluation methodology and harmonized specifications for labeling and data formats by 2025.

entries.title: UNECE R136 and EU Batteries Regulation - E-Moped Battery Compliance
entries.summary: L-category vehicles require UNECE R136 type approval for electric powertrain and REESS. EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542 introduces lifecycle obligations including labeling, durability classifications, and carbon-footprint disclosure. Additional directives include EMC and substance restrictions (RoHS/REACH).

entries.summary: As of August 1, 2025, RED compliance is mandatory for IoT devices with radio interfaces. Privacy assets must be identified and protected through security assets like TLS encryption and controlled access mechanisms before EN 18031-1 requirements can be assessed.

entries.title: Joint Industry Guidance on Battery Manufacturer Definition under EU Batteries Regulation

Supply chain mapping remains the biggest challenge as most companies lack visibility beyond tier two suppliers.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation: Due Diligence Requires Traceability - Material Traceability by August 2025
entries.summary: Economic operators must implement traceability systems by August 2025 for cobalt, natural graphite, lithium, and nickel supply chains to meet due diligence obligations under the EU Battery Regulation. Building reliable chain of custody requires end-to-end traceability with third-party verification.

entries.title: ESG Quick Guide: EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation - Due Diligence Elements
entries.summary: The EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation 2023 imposes due diligence requirements for batteries placed on the EU market, including sustainability, safety, labelling, and extended producer responsibility obligations. entries.title: The Real Stakes for Compliance Professionals With the EU Battery Regulation
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation represents lifecycle regulation governing batteries from raw material sourcing to recycling, integrating sustainability metrics, carbon accounting, supply chain due diligence, and digital traceability into market access requirements. entries.title: Supply Chain Due Diligence for Batteries - Market Environment and Regulatory Pressure

entries.title: RoHS Exemptions Review and Updates 2026
entries.summary: EU RoHS landscape undergoing significant updates in 2026 with changes to critical exemptions and convergence with PFAS restrictions, digital product passports, and circular economy requirements. entries.title: RoHS UV Mercury Vapor Lamp Exemption Expiration - 2027
entries.summary: The RoHS exemption for UV mercury vapor lamps is set to expire in 2027. This exemption, specified in Annex III of the RoHS directive, allows mercury concentrations above the standard 0.1% limit. Manufacturers using mercury in UV applications must prepare for compliance after the exemption expires.

entries.title: Delegated Directive (EU) 2015/863 - RoHS 3 Phthalate Restrictions

entries.title: Brazil Draft RoHS Regulation 2026

entries.title: WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU - Open Scope Amendment
entries.summary: The WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU introduced open scope on 15 August 2018, making all electrical and electronic equipment subject to compulsory registration. entries.title: UK WEEE Regulations 2025 Amendments - Online Marketplace Operators

entries.title: EU Universal Charger Directive Implementation Deadline
entries.summary: European Union's Universal Charger Directive requires all portable electronic devices sold in EU to use USB-C interfaces and be compatible with USB PD fast charging protocol. Deadline for laptop compliance certification is April 28, 2026.

entries.title: Guidelines for Interpretation of Directive on Universal Chargers
entries.source: Official Journal of the European Union
entries.summary: EU Commission clarification that RED requires USB-C port only for cable-charged devices; wireless charging and other methods remain permissible. Directive 2022/2380 allows flexibility for alternative charging technologies.

entries.title: External Power Supply Ecodesign Compliance Requirements

entries.title: IEC 63652 Wireless Charging Standards Recognition
entries.summary: International Electrotechnical Commission formally recognized NFC Wireless Charging under IEC 63652 for sub-3W devices. EU's Common Charging Directive calls for harmonized wireless charging standards development.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 - New Labelling and Collection Requirements
entries.summary: In 2026, new provisions of EU Batteries Regulation come into force imposing stricter labelling requirements including 'non-rechargeable' marking and duration of use. Higher collection targets (73% for portable batteries by 2030) and recycling efficiency targets (90% for key metals, 50% for lithium by 31.12.2027) are mandated.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 - Digital Battery Passport Implementation
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation applies to all batteries placed on the EU market, replacing the old Battery Directive. From 18 February 2027, electric vehicle and industrial batteries with capacity above 2kWh require a mandatory unique Digital Battery Passport (DBP) for placement on the EU market.

entries.title: Council of the European Union - Updated Measuring Instruments Directive for Electric Chargers
entries.summary: The new measuring instruments directive sets common standards for electric chargers and gas dispensers, clearing the path for widespread deployment of charging infrastructure. This supports Europe's transition to greener and more energy-efficient mobility systems.

entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation - Sustainability and Lifecycle Management Requirements
entries.summary: Regulation EU 2023/1542 establishes new sustainability and recycling requirements with carbon footprint evaluation methodology. Multiple requirements were mandated for 2025 adoption including harmonized specifications on labeling, data formats, and reporting to ensure consistency across the battery value chain.

entries.title: EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation - Due Diligence and ESG Compliance
entries.summary: The Sustainable Batteries Regulation 2023 imposes requirements on entities placing batteries on the EU market, mandating due diligence policies and management systems to identify and address social and environmental risks in raw material sourcing and processing. It repeals and replaces the Batteries Directive 2006.

entries.title: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 - Radio Equipment Directive Cybersecurity Requirements
entries.summary: Binding cybersecurity requirements for all radio equipment including IoT devices, wearables, and machines with integrated radio modules became active August 1, 2025. entries.title: EN 18031 Compliance - EU Radio Equipment Directive Cybersecurity Standards
entries.summary: EN 18031 series cybersecurity standards (covering network protection EN 18031-1, personal data protection EN 18031-2, and financial transaction security EN 18031-3) became mandatory for all internet-connected radio equipment placed on EU market since August 1, 2025. entries.title: RED Cybersecurity Requirements for IP Audio and PA Systems
entries.summary: EU Radio Equipment Directive enforces new cybersecurity requirements under Articles 3.3(d), (e), and (f) via Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 effective August 1, 2025. entries.summary: RED Article 3.3 addressing security of radio interfaces became effective February 1, 2022, with mandatory compliance required from August 1, 2025. entries.title: Shipping EV Batteries from China to Germany - HS Code and Import Duties
entries.summary: Lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles are classified under HS code 8507.60 with EU import taxes ranging from 1.9% to 3.7%, plus 19% VAT in Germany. Importers must use exact HS codes from EU TARIC database to avoid duty miscalculation and fines.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Digital Battery Passport and Traceability Requirements
entries.summary: EU Battery Regulation requires digital battery passport, traceability of raw materials, and carbon footprint reporting throughout the battery lifecycle. entries.title: UN 38.3 Testing and Safety Documentation Requirements for Lithium Batteries
entries.summary: EU customs requires UN 38.3 test reports (not older than 5 years from accredited labs) and Battery Safety Data Sheets citing UN 3480 for lithium-ion batteries. Documentation must clearly state battery model, test conditions, and hazard classification to avoid customs delays.

entries.title: Lithium Battery Classification and Compliance Labeling for EU Customs
entries.summary: Portable chargers must display battery chemistry (Li-ion or Li-polymer), RoHS and WEEE symbols on packaging, and classify watt-hour (Wh) ratings per UN 3480/3481. Batteries exceeding 100Wh require special handling; mAh listings alone are insufficient for customs verification.

entries.title: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for Batteries and Accumulators
entries.summary: EU EPR system assigns producers responsibility for collection, recycling, and disposal of batteries and accumulators after end-of-life. EPR aims to reduce waste, promote recyclable design, increase recovery rates, and shift environmental responsibility from public resources to manufacturers.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Chapter VII Due Diligence Obligations
entries.summary: Chapter VII of the EU Battery Regulation (EUBR) imposes due diligence obligations on economic operators placing batteries on the market, requiring risk-based environmental and human rights due diligence policies for supply chains of cobalt, natural graphite, lithium, and nickel for batteries above 2 kWh capacity. Companies must establish grievance mechanisms based on UN Guiding Principles.

entries.title: EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation 2023 - Supply Chain Due Diligence Elements
entries.summary: The EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation 2023, as amended by Omnibus IV, includes comprehensive due diligence elements (Chapter VII) alongside obligations for sustainability, safety, labelling, marking, information provision, and extended producer responsibility. The regulation governs batteries from raw material sourcing through recycling.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Lifecycle Governance and Sustainability Requirements
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation (2023/1542) establishes lifecycle regulation integrating sustainability metrics, carbon accounting, supply chain due diligence, and digital traceability as market access requirements. It expands scope beyond waste obligations to cover raw material sourcing, manufacturing, use-phase performance, repurposing, and recycling.

entries.title: Battery Passport Compliance and Non-Compliance Penalties
entries.summary: Missing or incomplete battery passport data can result in financial penalties, regulatory intervention, and restrictions on placing products on the European market. Battery passport requirements are now a strategic priority for manufacturers, importers, and battery value chain partners.

entries.title: Supply Chain Due Diligence for Batteries - Implementation Timeline
entries.summary: The EUBR due diligence obligations have been postponed by two years but remain mandatory. Economic operators must prepare for supply chain due diligence requirements covering cobalt, lithium, natural graphite, and nickel in a challenging market environment.

new_entries.title: Shipping EV Batteries from China to Germany - HS Code and Import Duties
new_entries.summary: Lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles are classified under HS code 8507.60 with EU import taxes ranging from 1.9% to 3.7%, plus 19% VAT in Germany. Importers must use exact HS codes from EU TARIC database to avoid duty miscalculation and fines.

new_entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Digital Battery Passport and Traceability Requirements
new_entries.summary: EU Battery Regulation requires digital battery passport, traceability of raw materials, and carbon footprint reporting throughout the battery lifecycle. The regulation aims to improve battery design, production, transportation, use and recycling while increasing transparency about materials and manufacturing standards.

new_entries.title: UN 38.3 Testing and Safety Documentation Requirements for Lithium Batteries
new_entries.summary: EU customs requires UN 38.3 test reports (not older than 5 years from accredited labs) and Battery Safety Data Sheets citing UN 3480 for lithium-ion batteries. Documentation must clearly state battery model, test conditions, and hazard classification to avoid customs delays.

new_entries.title: Lithium Battery Classification and Compliance Labeling for EU Customs
new_entries.summary: Portable chargers must display battery chemistry (Li-ion or Li-polymer), RoHS and WEEE symbols on packaging, and classify watt-hour (Wh) ratings per UN 3480/3481. Batteries exceeding 100Wh require special handling; mAh listings alone are insufficient for customs verification.

new_entries.title: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for Batteries and Accumulators
new_entries.summary: EU EPR system assigns producers responsibility for collection, recycling, and disposal of batteries and accumulators after end-of-life. EPR aims to reduce waste, promote recyclable design, increase recovery rates, and shift environmental responsibility from public resources to manufacturers.

new_entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Chapter VII Due Diligence Obligations
new_entries.summary: Chapter VII of the EU Battery Regulation (EUBR) imposes due diligence obligations on economic operators placing batteries on the market, requiring risk-based environmental and human rights due diligence policies for supply chains of cobalt, natural graphite, lithium, and nickel for batteries above 2 kWh capacity. Companies must establish grievance mechanisms based on UN Guiding Principles.

new_entries.title: EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation 2023 - Supply Chain Due Diligence Elements
new_entries.summary: The EU Sustainable Batteries Regulation 2023, as amended by Omnibus IV, includes comprehensive due diligence elements (Chapter VII) alongside obligations for sustainability, safety, labelling, marking, information provision, and extended producer responsibility. The regulation governs batteries from raw material sourcing through recycling.

new_entries.title: EU Battery Regulation - Lifecycle Governance and Sustainability Requirements
new_entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation (2023/1542) establishes lifecycle regulation integrating sustainability metrics, carbon accounting, supply chain due diligence, and digital traceability as market access requirements. It expands scope beyond waste obligations to cover raw material sourcing, manufacturing, use-phase performance, repurposing, and recycling.

entries.summary: RoHS declaration confirming compliance with EU hazardous substance restrictions including lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE, and phthalates (DEHP, BBP). Restrictions effective since July 1, 2006 with amendments through July 22, 2019.

entries.title: Key RoHS Exemptions Set for Major Changes
entries.summary: Nine critical RoHS exemptions are undergoing major regulatory changes. Manufacturers relying on current exemptions should review compliance strategies as exemption provisions are being revised under the EU RoHS directive.

entries.title: RoHS and REACH Compliance Requirements for EU Electronics
entries.summary: Overview of RoHS 2 (Directive 2011/65/EU) compliance requirements including restricted substances and maximum concentration values (MCVs). Covers seven hazardous substances with 0.1% weight limits (0.01% for cadmium) in homogeneous materials.

entries.title: Brazil Issues 2026 Draft Resolution for RoHS Regulation
entries.summary: Brazil proposes new RoHS regulation closely based on EU Directive 2011/65/EU to restrict 10 hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment. Relevant for manufacturers exporting to Brazilian market.

entries.title: UK WEEE Guidance Update: AATFs and PCSs Clarified
entries.summary: The UK Environment Agency updated WEEE guidance on evidence and national protocols, introducing clarifications on the relationship between Approved Authorised Treatment Facilities (AATFs) and Producer Compliance Schemes (PCSs). The update includes clearer expectations around contractual agreements and more detailed guidance on compliant evidence notes.

entries.title: EU WEEE EPR Regulations Update 2026
entries.summary: Significant updates to European WEEE and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations expected around 2026, particularly affecting medical device manufacturers. The update addresses alignment with evolving EU waste management and circular economy requirements.

entries.title: The 2025 WEEE Amendments - Online Marketplace Operators as Producers
entries.summary: The Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (Amendment, etc.) Regulations 2025 introduced significant changes including designation of online marketplace operators as producers. Additional amendments include vape retailer obligations effective 1 January 2024 and record-keeping requirements for distributors.

entries.title: Amending the Critical Raw Materials Act - WEEE Directive Exemptions
entries.summary: DIGITALEUROPE recommends amendments to the Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) to address overlaps with WEEE Directive requirements and recognize exemptions for medical devices that cannot be safely dismantled. The recommendation addresses regulatory conflicts between CRMA, ESPR, and WEEE Directive.

entries.title: EU Laptops Must Support USB-C Charging by April 2026
entries.summary: From 28 April 2026, laptops placed on the EU market must support USB-C charging under Directive (EU) 2022/2380. This regulation standardizes charging ports across consumer electronics and reduces electronic waste from incompatible chargers. Fast-charging technologies must work consistently with compatible chargers.

entries.title: EU Common Charger Directive - Universal USB-C Standardization
entries.summary: The Council and European Parliament reached a provisional political agreement on a directive making USB-C charging mandatory for a range of electronic devices. Implementation required 24 months after entry into force, improving consumer convenience and reducing electronic waste. Consumers may purchase devices with or without chargers.

entries.title: Ecodesign Requirements for External Power Supplies
entries.summary: EU ecodesign regulations establish requirements for external power supplies, part of the broader Energy-Related Products (ErP) Directive framework. Requirements include efficiency standards and standby power consumption limits for power adapters sold in EU markets.

entries.title: EU Standardizes USB-C Chargers and External Power Supply Standards
entries.summary: The European Commission's USB-C common charger framework requires harmonized power specifications and Type-C interfaces for electronic devices sold in EU. Manufacturers must deliver high power density designs, energy efficiency compliance, and safety standards for external switching power supplies.

entries.title: Guidelines for Interpretation of Universal Chargers Directive
entries.summary: Official Journal of the European Union C/2024/2997 clarifies that Directive (EU) 2022/2380 requires USB-C port only for cable-charged devices. Wireless charging and other methods remain permissible, with the Commission monitoring future developments for potential regulatory action.

entries.title: EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 - Implementation and Compliance Requirements
entries.summary: The EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 replaces Directive 2006/66/EC and introduces stricter requirements for battery safety, sustainability, transparency, and lifecycle management. Full implementation with digital battery passport requirements begins February 2027, with intensified design and durability rules effective in 2026.

entries.title: Right to Repair Directive - Battery Replaceability Requirements
entries.summary: The Right to Repair directive, passed in 2024, becomes law in July 2026 and mandates that rechargeable batteries in consumer devices must be easily replaceable without special tools. This applies to portable chargers, smartphones, gaming devices, and other battery-containing consumer electronics.

entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation - Recycling Efficiency and Material Recovery Rates Methodology
entries.summary: Position paper on improvements to draft delegated act for calculating recycling efficiencies and material recovery rates under the Batteries Regulation. Addresses methodology updates for compliance with EU 2023/1542 requirements.

entries.title: EU Batteries Regulation - Digital Battery Passport Implementation
entries.summary: EU Regulation 2023/1542 establishes requirements for digital battery passports providing lifecycle information for all batteries and cells on the EU market. Applies to EV batteries, light means of transport batteries, and industrial batteries with comprehensive data transparency requirements starting February 2027.

entries.title: Battery Labeling and CE Marking Requirements for EU Market Entry
entries.summary: EU regulations require portable chargers and battery-containing devices to display nominal voltage, capacity, and watt-hour ratings visibly on units with verified CE marking. Lithium-ion batteries must comply with UN classification and transport regulations for EU market access.

entries.title: FAA GPS/GNSS Interference Resource Guide Version 1.1
entries.summary: The FAA released an updated GPS/GNSS Interference Resource Guide addressing jamming and spoofing trends, impacts on aircraft systems, and pilot procedures. The guide responds to a surge in GNSS interference events affecting aviation safety across European and global airspace.

entries.title: EASA-IATA Four-Workstream Action Plan for GNSS Interference
entries.summary: EASA and IATA jointly issued a comprehensive four-point action plan addressing GNSS disruptions in European airspace, including standardized radio call procedures, real-time monitoring, jamming device controls, and spoofing detection systems. The plan responds to a 220% increase in GPS signal-loss events between 2021-2024.

entries.title: GNSS Resilience as Economic and Security Priority in Europe
entries.summary: Analysis of GNSS disruption affecting over 5% of commercial flights in Europe, with deliberate interference on the rise. The report highlights economic and security implications, including recent incidents affecting EU leadership aircraft.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive (RED) - CE Mark Requirements for Walkie Talkies
entries.summary: CE mark is mandatory for walkie talkies sold in EEA under RED and EMC Directives. Products must comply with EU health, safety, and environmental protection standards. Consumers should verify CE mark presence when purchasing two-way radios for professional or commercial purposes in Europe.

entries.title: ATEX Directive 2014/34/EU - Hazardous Environment Radio Equipment Certification
entries.summary: ATEX Directive 2014/34/EU establishes certification requirements for radio equipment used in hazardous environments (Zone 1 and Zone 2). Explosion-proof PoC radios must be certified for use in locations with flammable substances such as oil refineries, chemical plants, and mining operations.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive - Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 Cybersecurity Requirements
entries.summary: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 on the Radio Equipment Directive (RED) has been active since August 1, 2025, mandating binding cybersecurity compliance for all radio equipment including IoT devices, wearables, and smart toys. Manufacturers must apply harmonized standards EN 18031-1/2/3 to ensure devices do not cause harmful effects on networks or misuse of resources.

entries.title: EN 18031 Cybersecurity Certification for Radio Equipment - Market Access Requirements
entries.summary: SGS has certified connected radio products to the EN 18031 standard under EU Radio Equipment Directive requirements, demonstrating that manufacturers must achieve full compliance with Articles 3.3(d), (e) and (f) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30. Early engagement in the compliance process identifies potential issues and improves efficiency during testing and evaluation.

entries.title: OTA Security and RED Cybersecurity Requirements for Connected Products
entries.summary: The Radio Equipment Directive cybersecurity delegated act requires manufacturers to ensure transparent inventory of third-party components and define three essential security capabilities: authentication of software execution, firmware integrity verification, and update tampering detection. Requirements apply throughout device lifecycle for OTA-capable systems.

entries.title: EN 18031-1 Security Compliance Assessment Tool for IoT and Radio Products
entries.summary: ByteSnap Design has unveiled an EN 18031-1 Cybersecurity Requirements Assessment tool to help manufacturers prepare internet-connected radio products for EU market launch in 2026 and beyond. The tool provides guidance aligned with EN 18031, IEC 62443, ETSI EN 303 645 standards and emphasizes cybersecurity-by-design principles.

entries.title: CNLABS Validates Compliance with EU RED Article 3.3 EN 18031 Requirements
entries.summary: CNLABS has completed cybersecurity conformity testing validating multiple product lines for EU RED compliance with EN 18031 harmonized standards, covering network protection, personal data protection, and fraud prevention. Technical Evidence Dossiers support CE marking and regulatory acceptance for radio equipment.

entries.title: ETSI TS 133 127 - 5G Lawful Interception Architecture and Functions
entries.summary: 3GPP technical specification for 5G system lawful interception architecture and functions (Release 19). This standard addresses security and interception procedures for 5G telecommunications systems.

entries.title: ETSI TS 133 501 - 5G Security Architecture and Procedures
entries.summary: 3GPP technical specification defining security architecture and procedures for 5G System (Release 15). Critical for radio equipment compliance with 5G security requirements under RED directive.

entries.title: Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2014/53/EU Compliance Requirements
entries.summary: EU Radio Equipment Directive establishing harmonized standards for GSM, 4G, and 5G radio equipment compliance. Devices must meet RED requirements along with EMC and LVD directives.

entries.summary: New binding European regulations creating uniform cybersecurity requirements for networked systems including 5G modules and radio equipment throughout their lifecycle. Applies to software, hardware and operational processes.

entries.summary: EU Radio Equipment Directive (RED) introduces mandatory cybersecurity requirements affecting wireless products using Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and other wireless technologies. Webinar covers affected products, cybersecurity requirement scope, and manufacturer preparation strategies.

entries.title: ETSI EN 300 328 - 2.4 GHz ISM Band Spectrum Usage Compliance

entries.title: ETSI EN 301 489-17 - EMC Requirements for Bluetooth/WiFi Equipment
